tools.name: Moving truck size calculator
tools.title: Moving Truck Size Calculator: What Size Truck Do I Need?
tools.q: What size truck fits everything I own?
tools.desc: Count your furnished rooms and big items, and see which rental truck size fits, how full it will be and what the load weighs.
fields: Bedrooms, living room, dining room, office. Skip bathrooms and halls.
Extra boxes beyond a normal household
Book collections, hobby gear, a home business
tools.how:
A fully furnished room takes roughly 150 to 200 cubic feet of truck space once the furniture and its boxes are stacked. The calculator multiplies your room count by the figure you pick, adds 35 cubic feet for each large appliance, 3 cubic feet for each extra medium box, and an allowance for garage and patio items.

Nobody loads a truck perfectly, so the total is divided by a loading factor: 1.0 for tight professional stacking, 0.9 for a careful first-timer, 0.8 if you have many odd shapes. The result is matched to the smallest common rental size that holds it: cargo van (about 245 cu ft), 10 ft (400), 12 ft (450), 15 to 16 ft (760), 20 ft (1,000), 22 ft (1,200) and 26 ft (1,650).

Weight is estimated at 7 pounds per cubic foot of household goods, the rule of thumb long-distance movers use for planning. Example: 5 average rooms and 3 appliances come to 980 cu ft of goods, 1,089 cu ft of truck space at average stacking, so a 22 ft truck at 91% full. That is tight enough that the 26 ft truck is the safer booking.
faq: Should I size up if I am between two trucks?

Yes, when the gauge is above about 90%. A second trip or a last-minute trailer costs more than the price gap between two truck sizes, and a slightly empty truck is easy to brace with blankets and straps.
Do bedrooms alone tell me the truck size?
Not well. A one-bedroom home with an office, a full dining room and a packed garage can outgrow a truck sized for two bedrooms. Count every furnished room.
Can a rental truck carry the weight?
Usually, for household goods. Dense loads such as books, tools, gym plates or stone are the exception. Compare the estimated weight with the payload printed on the truck door or the rental agreement.

tools.name: DIY moving cost calculator
tools.title: DIY Moving Cost Calculator: Truck, Fuel, Help and Supplies
tools.q: What will a do-it-yourself move really cost?
tools.desc: Build a full budget for a rental-truck move, with fuel priced from this week's national averages, and compare it with a mover's quote.
fields: Filled in from this week's survey. Type over it if your pump price differs.
tools.how:
The budget adds six lines: truck rental (days times daily rate, plus miles times the mileage charge), fuel (miles divided by miles per gallon, times the pump price), paid help (helpers times hours times hourly rate), damage cover, supplies and travel extras.

The starting numbers are placeholders so the form is not empty. They are not a price list. Rental pricing varies by city, season and day of the week, so copy the figures from your own reservation. For a one-way rental quoted as a flat price with miles included, enter the flat price as the daily rate for one day and set the mileage charge to zero.

The fuel price is filled in from the latest U.S. Energy Information Administration weekly survey for the region you pick. Box trucks commonly return 6 to 12 miles per gallon loaded; the rental company lists the figure for each size.
faq: Is a DIY move always cheaper than hiring movers?

For a local move, usually. For a long one-way move the gap narrows once you add fuel, lodging, several rental days and time off work. Enter a mover's quote in the last field to see the difference for your move.
What costs do people forget?
Refuelling to the pickup level, damage cover, furniture pads and a hand truck, tolls for a commercial-height vehicle, and parking permits in dense cities.
How many helpers do I need?
Two people can load a one or two bedroom home in a few hours. For three bedrooms or more, a third pair of hands shortens the day more than it adds to the bill.

tools.name: Packing box calculator
tools.title: Packing Box Calculator: How Many Moving Boxes Do I Need?
tools.q: How many boxes should I buy?
tools.desc: Get a starting count of small, medium, large and wardrobe boxes, plus tape, from the rooms and people in your home.
fields: A lot, or many years in the same home
tools.how:
The count uses a plain rule you can check by hand: a set number of boxes per furnished room (8, 12 or 16 depending on how much you own) plus five per person for clothes, shoes and personal things. The total is split 40% small, 35% medium and 25% large, because heavy items belong in small boxes and only light, bulky items should go in large ones.

Wardrobe boxes are counted at one and a half per person, and tape at one roll per fifteen boxes. Standard sizes are assumed: small 1.5 cubic feet, medium 3.0 and large 4.5. The last line shows the truck space those boxes will take, which you can carry over to the truck size calculator.
faq: Is it better to have too many boxes or too few?
Too many. Running out on packing night costs you time you do not have. Many sellers refund unused boxes, and neighbours take the rest.
Can I use free boxes from shops?
For light items, yes. Mixed sizes stack badly in a truck, though, and tired cardboard crushes at the bottom of a stack. Use new, same-size boxes for anything heavy or fragile.

tools.name: Moving checklist
tools.title: Moving Checklist: Eight Weeks Out to Unloading Day
tools.q: What should I be doing this week?
tools.desc: A week-by-week moving checklist that saves your ticks on this device and prints on a single sheet.
tools.how:
Tick items as you finish them. Your progress is stored in this browser only, so it is still here when you come back on the same device, and nothing is sent to us. Use Print for a paper copy to tape inside a cupboard door.

The order follows how lead times work in practice: trucks, containers and movers book up first, paperwork and address changes take weeks to settle, and packing always takes longer than planned. If your move is closer than eight weeks, start at the top anyway and work down quickly.
faq: When should I book a truck or movers?
As early as you can fix the date. The end of each month and the summer season sell out first, and prices climb as the date gets close.

tools.name: Payload calculator
tools.title: Payload Calculator: How Much Weight Can My Truck Carry?
tools.q: How much can my pickup carry with people aboard?
tools.desc: Subtract passengers, gear and trailer tongue weight from your truck's payload rating and see how much cargo you can still add.
fields: If you enter this, the two fields below are ignored.
tools.how:
Payload is everything the vehicle carries on its own wheels: people, cargo, accessories and the downward weight of any trailer on the hitch. The rating is GVWR minus curb weight. The yellow tire and loading sticker inside the driver door states it for your exact truck as it left the factory, in a sentence that begins "The combined weight of occupants and cargo should never exceed". That figure beats any brochure number, because options such as four-wheel drive and a larger cab eat into payload.

The calculator subtracts what you enter from the rating and shows what is left. Example: a 1,700 lb rating, two adults at 350 lb, a 100 lb bed cover and 600 lb of tongue weight leave 650 lb for the bed.
faq: Is payload the same as towing capacity?
No. Payload is carried, towing capacity is pulled. They interact because a trailer's tongue weight is carried by the truck and uses up payload.
Do passengers really count?
Yes. Four adults can use 700 lb or more of a half-ton pickup's payload before anything goes in the bed.
What happens if I go over?
Longer stopping distances, overheated brakes and tires, sagging rear suspension and light steering. It can also create liability after a crash.

tools.name: Towing capacity calculator
tools.title: Towing Capacity Calculator: Can My Vehicle Pull This Trailer?
tools.q: Can I safely pull this trailer?
tools.desc: Find the heaviest trailer your setup can pull from its weakest link, and the tongue weight to aim for.
fields: With fuel, people and cargo aboard
Lowest of receiver, ball mount and ball
tools.how:
Three numbers can each cap what you tow. The first is the gross combined weight rating minus the actual loaded weight of the tow vehicle: the more you put in the truck, the less trailer it can pull. The second is the maker's tow rating. The third is the hitch, which is only as strong as its lowest-rated piece. The calculator takes the smallest of the three and compares your loaded trailer against it.

It also shows a target for tongue weight: 10 to 15% of trailer weight for a bumper-pull trailer and 15 to 25% for a fifth wheel or gooseneck. Too little weight on the hitch is the classic cause of trailer sway. Too much overloads the rear axle and lifts weight off the steering wheels.
faq: Where do I find GCWR?
In the towing section of the owner's manual or the maker's towing guide for your model year, engine and axle ratio. It is usually not on the door sticker.
How do I weigh my setup?
A public truck scale weighs the tow vehicle and trailer for a small fee. Weigh the truck alone, then the truck and trailer together, and subtract.
Does a weight-distribution hitch raise my tow rating?
No. It spreads tongue weight across the axles and improves control, but the vehicle's ratings stay the same.

tools.name: Tie-down calculator
tools.title: Tie-Down Calculator: How Many Straps or Chains Do I Need?
tools.q: How many straps does this load need?
tools.desc: Work out the minimum number of straps or chains for a piece of cargo from its weight, its length and the working load limit of your tie-downs.
fields: Working load limit of each tie-down
Printed on the strap tag or stamped on the chain
Over or around the cargo, hooked to the vehicle on both sides
From a vehicle anchor straight to an anchor on the cargo
Cargo is butted against a bulkhead or other cargo so it cannot slide forward
tools.how:
The calculator applies the two tests in the U.S. cargo securement rules for commercial vehicles and shows the larger answer.

Strength. The working load limits of all tie-downs added together must equal at least half the weight of the cargo. A strap that passes over the cargo and hooks to the vehicle on both sides counts for its full limit. A strap or chain that runs from one anchor on the vehicle to an anchor on the cargo counts for half.

Count. For cargo that is not blocked from sliding forward: one tie-down if it is 5 ft or shorter and 1,100 lb or lighter; two if it is 5 ft or shorter but heavier, or between 5 and 10 ft; and two plus one more for every further 10 ft, or part of 10 ft, beyond the first 10. Cargo blocked at the front needs one for every 10 ft or part of 10 ft.

Example: a 1,500 lb machine 8 ft long with 500 lb straps over the top needs 750 lb of total limit, so two straps by strength and two by length. Two is the minimum.
faq: Is working load limit the same as breaking strength?
No. Working load limit is the safe working figure, commonly one third of breaking strength. Packaging often prints the larger breaking number in big type. Plan with the limit.
Do these rules apply to my pickup or utility trailer?

The federal rule covers commercial motor vehicles. Every state also requires any vehicle's load to be secured so nothing can fall or shift, so the commercial minimums are a sensible floor for everyone.
What else matters besides the count?
Protect straps from sharp edges, pull opposite corners in opposite directions, and re-check tension after the first few miles, when loads settle.

tools.name: Gravel, soil and mulch load calculator
tools.title: Gravel, Soil and Mulch Calculator: Cubic Yards, Weight and Truckloads
tools.q: How many yards do I need, and how many trips?
tools.desc: Turn the area you are covering into cubic yards, weight and the number of pickup trips, without overloading the truck.
fields: Door-jamb sticker figure minus the people aboard
Bed or trailer volume, filled level
About 1.5 for a short bed, 2.5 for an 8 ft bed
tools.how:
Volume is length times width times depth, with depth converted from inches to feet, divided by 27 to give cubic yards. Weight is volume times a typical density for the material: about 2,800 lb per cubic yard for gravel, 2,700 for sand, 2,200 for topsoil, 2,000 for fill dirt, 2,500 for broken concrete, 1,400 for compost, 700 for bark mulch and 550 for wood chips.

The number of trips is set by whichever runs out first, bed volume or payload. For stone, sand and soil it is nearly always payload: a level short bed of gravel weighs about two tons, far beyond what a half-ton pickup may carry. The gauge shows how a level bed of your material compares with your payload, and the warning tells you what share of the bed to ask the yard to fill.
faq: How much gravel can a half-ton pickup carry?
Typically about half a cubic yard, which looks like very little in the bed. Mulch is the opposite: a full, heaped bed is usually within payload.
Why is my delivered weight higher than this?
Moisture. Rain-soaked topsoil or sand can weigh 20% or more above the dry figure. Leave a margin after wet weather.
Is delivery cheaper than hauling it myself?
Often, beyond two or three cubic yards. Compare the delivery fee with your trips multiplied by fuel and time.

tools.name: Trip fuel cost calculator
tools.title: Trip Fuel Cost Calculator With This Week's Gas and Diesel Prices
tools.q: What will the fuel cost for this haul?
tools.desc: Price the fuel for any haul using this week's regional gasoline and diesel averages, updated automatically.
fields: From this week's survey. Type over it to use your pump price.
Optional, to see range and fill-ups
tools.how:
Fuel burned is distance divided by miles per gallon, and cost is gallons times the price per gallon. The price field fills itself from the latest weekly retail survey by the U.S. Energy Information Administration for the fuel and region you choose, and this site refreshes that figure on a schedule. Type your own pump price over it at any time.

The number that matters most is loaded fuel economy. A pickup that returns 20 mpg empty may see 10 to 12 with a tall trailer behind it, and rental box trucks commonly return 6 to 12. If you add a tank size, the ticket also shows range per tank and the number of fill-ups to plan.
faq: Which region am I in?

East Coast runs from Maine to Florida. Midwest covers the Great Lakes and Plains states plus Kentucky, Tennessee and Oklahoma. Gulf Coast is Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Arkansas and New Mexico. Rocky Mountain is Colorado, Utah, Wyoming, Montana and Idaho. West Coast is everything further west, with Alaska and Hawaii.
How do I measure loaded fuel economy?
Fill up, reset the trip meter, drive loaded, fill up again, and divide miles driven by gallons added.

tools.name: Cubic feet calculator
tools.title: Cubic Feet Calculator for Boxes, Furniture and Freight
tools.q: How much space does this item take?
tools.desc: Convert the length, width and height of anything into cubic feet, cubic yards, cubic metres and litres, with density if you know the weight.
tools.how:
Volume is length times width times height. In inches, divide the product by 1,728 to get cubic feet, because a cubic foot is 12 by 12 by 12 inches. Divide cubic feet by 27 for cubic yards, or multiply by 0.0283 for cubic metres.

For freight and moving, measure the outside of the packed item at its longest, widest and tallest points, including pallets, feet and handles. Space is sold as a box around the item, not the item itself. Enter a weight to see density in pounds per cubic foot, the figure that drives freight class.
faq: How many cubic feet is a standard pallet?
A 48 by 40 inch pallet loaded 48 inches high is 53.3 cubic feet. At 36 inches high it is 40.
How do I measure something that is not a box?
Imagine the smallest box it would fit inside and measure that. Carriers and movers do the same.

tools.name: Freight class calculator
tools.title: Freight Class Calculator: Density to LTL Class on the 13-Step Scale
tools.q: What LTL freight class is my shipment?
tools.desc: Enter dimensions and weight to get shipment density and its estimated LTL freight class on the current 13-step density scale.
tools.how:
Density is weight divided by volume. The calculator multiplies length, width and height in inches, divides by 1,728 for cubic feet, then divides the weight by that volume. The class is read from the standard density scale that less-than-truckload carriers use:

Pounds per cubic footClass
Less than 1400
1 to under 2300
2 to under 4250
4 to under 6175
6 to under 8125
8 to under 10100
10 to under 1292.5
12 to under 1585
15 to under 22.570
22.5 to under 3065
30 to under 3560
35 to under 5055
50 or more50

The scale grew from 11 steps to 13 in July 2025, when classes 55 and 50 were added for the densest freight and many commodities moved to density-based classing. Lower class numbers cost less per hundred pounds. Example: a 48 by 40 by 48 inch pallet weighing 500 lb is 53.3 cubic feet and 9.4 lb per cubic foot, class 100.
faq: Is the result my official class?

It is an estimate from density alone. Some commodities are classed on handling, stowability or liability instead. The National Motor Freight Classification is the authority, and your carrier or broker can confirm the item number.
How can I lower my class?
Raise density. Remove empty space in cartons, avoid overhang, and build pallets tight and square. A shorter pallet with the same weight moves up the density scale.
What if the carrier measures something different?
The carrier's inspection wins and you are billed the difference, often with a fee. Measure the widest points and weigh the finished pallet.

tools.name: Pallet calculator
tools.title: Pallet Calculator: How Many Pallets Fit in a Truck, Trailer or Container?
tools.q: How many pallets fit in this trailer?
tools.desc: Count how many pallets fit on the floor of a trailer, box truck or container, straight or turned, and whether weight or space runs out first.
tools.how:
The floor count tries the pallets two ways: loaded straight, with the long side running the length of the trailer, and turned sideways. It keeps the better result. For standard 48 by 40 inch pallets in a 53 ft dry van that is 26 straight or 30 turned, the figures dispatchers quote from memory.

If pallets can be double stacked and you give a loaded height, a second tier is added when it fits under the roof. The count is then capped by weight: the payload limit divided by the weight of one pallet. The ticket tells you which limit binds. Dense freight weighs out with floor space to spare; light freight cubes out long before the scale complains.

Inside dimensions are typical for each equipment type. Payload defaults are conservative road figures, so change the limit to match the truck you have booked.
faq: Why does a 53 ft trailer rarely carry more than about 45,000 lb?
The 80,000 lb gross limit on U.S. interstates covers tractor, trailer and cargo together. An empty rig weighs roughly 33,000 to 36,000 lb.
Can I always turn pallets sideways?
Only if the forklift can enter from the 48 inch side, and the freight has no overhang. Ask the shipper and receiver before planning on 30.

tools.name: Box fit calculator
tools.title: Box Fit Calculator: How Many Boxes Fit in a Truck or Container?
tools.q: How many of these boxes fit in the truck?
tools.desc: See how many identical boxes fit in a box truck, trailer or container, the best way to face them, and when weight becomes the limit.
tools.how:
A box can face six ways. For each one the calculator counts how many whole boxes fit along the length, across the width and up the height of the space, multiplies the three, and keeps the best. Tick the upright option for liquids, plants or anything marked with arrows, and only the two upright layouts are tried.

The space count is then compared with the weight limit. Medium moving boxes at 30 lb each reach the payload of a 16 ft box truck at about 143 boxes, well before the cargo box is full. The gauge shows how much of the volume the final count uses.
faq: Why is the real number sometimes lower?
Wheel wells, a tapered roof, door hardware and bulging cartons all steal space. Take 5 to 10% off for anything other than rigid, uniform cartons.
Can mixing orientations fit more?
Sometimes a few, by turning the last row to fill a gap. Dedicated load-planning software does this; for planning a purchase or a rental, the single-orientation count is close.

tools.name: Cost per mile calculator
tools.title: Trucking Cost Per Mile Calculator and Load Profit Check
tools.desc: Find your true cost to run one mile as an owner-operator or small fleet, then test any load offer against it, deadhead included.
tools.how:
Cost per mile has two parts. Fixed costs are the bills that arrive whether the truck moves or not; divide the monthly total by the miles you actually drive. Variable costs rise with every mile: fuel (price per gallon divided by miles per gallon), maintenance and tires, and driver pay. Add them and you have the lowest rate at which a mile pays for itself.

The load check divides the offered rate by all miles, loaded plus deadhead, and subtracts your cost for those miles. A load paying $2.50 per loaded mile over 400 miles with 100 miles of deadhead really pays $2.00 across the 500 miles you drive.

The defaults are placeholders, not benchmarks. Use your own statements, and pay yourself in the driver line so that a profit is a profit and not just your wage.
faq: Why does driving more miles lower my cost per mile?
Fixed costs are spread over more miles. That only helps if the extra miles pay more than your variable cost.
Should I count my own pay as a cost?
Yes. If the truck only breaks even after you work for free, the business is losing money.
What else should I set aside?
Taxes, a maintenance reserve for major repairs, and downtime. Many operators add a few cents per mile for each.

tips: Load the heaviest items first, low and against the front wall of the truck, so the weight sits ahead of the rear axle.
Photograph the fuel gauge and odometer before you leave the rental lot. It settles most refuelling disputes.
A trailer wants about 60% of its cargo weight ahead of the axle. Too far back and it will sway at speed.
Check strap tension after the first 10 miles. Loads settle, and a strap that was tight in the driveway can be slack by the highway.
Stand mattresses and sofas on end against the truck wall and strap them. They become padding for everything else.
The payload on your door-jamb sticker includes the people in the cab. Four adults can use up half of it.
Never plan with a strap's breaking strength. The working load limit on the tag is the number that counts.
Fill the truck in tiers from floor to ceiling, front to back, and strap each tier before starting the next.
Put the things you need first at the new place on last: bedding, the kettle, tools, the toilet paper.
A level bed of gravel overloads a half-ton pickup several times over. Ask the yard to load by weight, not by eye.
Measure pallets at their widest point, including overhang. The carrier will, and you pay the difference.
Deadhead miles cost as much to drive as loaded ones. Divide the rate by all the miles before you say yes.
Disassemble bed frames and table legs and tape the hardware to the largest piece in a labelled bag.
Book trucks and movers for mid-month and mid-week if you can. The last weekend of the month is the most expensive time to move.
Cross your tie-downs so each one pulls against another. Two straps pulling the same way hold in only one direction.
Keep heavy boxes small. If a box takes two people to lift, repack it.
A ramp is steeper than it looks with a loaded dolly. Walk heavy items down backwards with a spotter below and to the side.
Weigh a loaded trailer at a public truck scale once. After that you know what your usual load weighs for good.
Protect straps from sharp corners with edge guards or folded cardboard. A cut strap has no working load limit at all.
Before signing with an interstate mover, look up its USDOT number in the federal mover database and read the complaint history.
Leave the fridge door propped open for a day before moving day so it is dry inside, and keep it upright in the truck.

Pack a first-night box: bedding, towels, chargers, medicines, kettle, tools
Defrost and dry the fridge and freezer
Disassemble beds and large furniture you can live without
Withdraw cash for tips and tolls
Loading day
Photograph the truck, fuel gauge and odometer at pickup
Protect floors and door frames before the first item moves
Load heaviest items first, low and to the front; strap each tier
Walk every room, cupboard, loft and shed before closing the truck
Read meters and hand over keys
Unloading day
Check for damage before signing any delivery paperwork
Unload the first-night box and build the beds first
Refuel the truck to the pickup level and photograph the gauge
Return the truck and equipment on time, and keep the receipt
glossary: The working load limits of every tie-down on a piece of cargo added together. U.S. commercial rules require it to be at least half the cargo's weight.
The most weight one axle may carry. A vehicle can be under its total rating and still overload one axle if the cargo sits in the wrong place.
The shipping document that acts as receipt, contract and description of the freight. Check piece count and condition before signing it at delivery.
A mover's written price that cannot rise unless you add items or services. A non-binding estimate can change with the actual weight.
A tractor driving without a trailer.
The front wall of a cargo area. Butting cargo against it stops forward movement.
To run out of space before reaching the weight limit. Light, bulky freight cubes out.
A vehicle's weight with fluids and a full tank but no people or cargo.
Miles driven empty, usually to reach the next pickup. They cost money and earn none.
Weight divided by volume, in pounds per cubic foot. It is the main driver of LTL freight class.
An enclosed, unrefrigerated trailer. The 53 ft dry van is the standard U.S. truckload trailer.
Material used to fill gaps and brace cargo: lumber, air bags, cardboard, blankets.
Steel rails on a cargo wall or floor with slots for strap fittings and load bars.
One of 18 classes from 50 to 500 that LTL carriers use to price freight. Lower classes are denser and cheaper to ship per pound.
A shipment that hires the whole trailer, moving straight from origin to destination.
Gross combined weight rating: the most a tow vehicle, its trailer and everything in both may weigh together.
Gross vehicle weight rating: the most a vehicle may weigh fully loaded, including people, fuel, cargo and tongue weight.
A two-wheeled upright dolly for boxes and appliances.
A company that arranges a move and hands it to a motor carrier. In the U.S. a broker for interstate moves must be registered with the federal regulator.
A powered platform at the back of a truck that raises freight from the ground. Carriers charge for it on LTL deliveries without a dock.
The length of trailer floor a shipment occupies. Long shipments can be priced by it instead of by class.
An adjustable bar that braces between cargo walls to keep freight from shifting.
Freight that shares a trailer with other shippers' freight and is priced by weight, class and distance.
The National Motor Freight Classification, the published standard that assigns freight classes to commodities.
The weight a vehicle can carry: GVWR minus curb weight. People, cargo and tongue weight all count.
The downward force a fifth-wheel or gooseneck trailer puts on the hitch in the truck bed.
A webbing tie-down tightened with a ratcheting buckle. Its working load limit is on the sewn-in tag.
The empty weight of a container, trailer or truck.
The downward force a bumper-pull trailer puts on the hitch ball. The usual target is 10 to 15% of trailer weight.
Side-to-side swinging of a trailer, most often caused by too little tongue weight or too much speed.
The identifier the U.S. Department of Transportation assigns to carriers and movers. Use it to look up registration and complaint records.
To reach the weight limit before running out of space. Dense freight weighs out.
A hitch with spring bars that shifts some tongue weight to the front axle and the trailer axles. It improves control without raising any rating.
The greatest load a strap, chain or anchor should carry in normal use, typically one third of its breaking strength.
